資治通鑑巻第二百一十四
Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 214
2
【唐紀三十】起閼逢閹茂，盡重光大荒落，凡八年。
[Tang Records 30] From the jianmao year through dahuoluo—eight years in all.
3
春，正月，己巳，上-{發}-西京； 己-{丑}-，至東都。 張九齡自韶州入見，求終喪； 不許。
In spring, the first month, on jisi, the Emperor set out from Chang'an; On jichou, he reached Luoyang. Zhang Jiuling came up from Shaozhou for an audience and asked to be allowed to finish his mourning obligations; The request was denied.
4
二月，壬寅，秦州地連震，壞公私屋殆盡，吏民壓死者四千-{餘}-人； 命左丞相蕭-{嵩}-賑恤。
In the second month, on renyin, a series of earthquakes struck Qinzhou, destroying almost all public and private buildings and killing more than four thousand officials and civilians; He ordered Left Chancellor Xiao Song to organize relief and aid.
5
方士張果自言有神仙-{術}-，誑人-{云}-堯時爲侍中，-{於}-今數千歳； 多往來恆山中，則天以來，屢-{-{征}-}-不至。 恆州刺史韋濟-{薦}-之，上遣中書-{舍}-人徐嶠繼璽書迎之。 庚寅，至東都，肩輿入宮，恩禮甚厚。
The Daoist adept Zhang Guo claimed supernatural powers and told people he had served as a palace attendant in the age of Yao and was now several thousand years old; He frequented Mount Heng, and since Empress Wu's time had been summoned many times but never appeared at court. Hengzhou prefect Wei Ji recommended him, and the Emperor sent Secretariat Drafter Xu Qiao with repeated imperial summons to escort him to court. On gengyin he reached Luoyang, was borne into the palace in a sedan chair, and was treated with exceptional honor.
6
張九齡請不禁鑄錢，三月，庚辰，敕百官議之。 裴耀卿等皆曰：「一啓此門，恐小人棄農逐利，而濫惡更甚。 」秘書監崔沔曰：「若稅銅折役，則官冶可成，計估度庸，則私鑄無利，易而可久，簡而難誣。 且夫錢之爲物，貴以通貨，利不在多，何待私鑄然-{後}-足用也！ 」右監門録事參軍劉秩曰：「夫人富則不可以賞勸，貧則不可以威禁，若許其私鑄，貧者必不能爲之； 臣恐貧者益貧而役-{於}-富，富者益富而逞其欲。 漢文帝時，呉王濞富埒天子，鑄錢所致也。 」上乃止。 秩，子玄之子也。
Zhang Jiuling had urged against lifting the ban on private coinage; in the third month, on gengchen, the Emperor ordered the court to debate the matter. Pei Yaoji and others argued: "Once that gate is opened, petty men will abandon farming for profit, and debased coin will only grow worse. " Director of the Palace Library Cui Hao said: "Tax copper and commute labor service, and official minting can work; assess levies by estimated corvée value, and private casting will not pay—simple, durable, and hard to cheat. Money exists to circulate goods; the point is not sheer volume—why must we rely on private casting before the supply is adequate? " Right Gatekeeper Record Officer Liu Zhi said: "The rich cannot be moved by rewards alone, nor the poor restrained by punishments alone. If private casting is allowed, the poor will never be able to do it; I fear the poor will only grow poorer in service to the rich, while the rich grow richer and indulge every appetite. Under Emperor Wen of Han, King Liu Pi of Wu grew as wealthy as the emperor himself—because he cast his own coin. " The Emperor dropped the proposal. Liu Zhi was a son of Liu Zixuan.
7
夏，四月，壬辰，以朔方節度使信安王禕兼關内道採訪處置使，增領涇、原等十二州。
In summer, the fourth month, on renchen, Prince Xin'an Li Yi, commissioner of Shuofang, was also appointed investigation and disposition commissioner for Guannei Circuit, gaining authority over twelve additional prefectures including Jing and Yuan.
8
吏部侍郎李林甫，柔佞多狡數，深結宦官及妃嬪家，侍候上動靜，無不知之。 由是毎奏對，常稱旨，上悅之。 時武惠妃寵幸傾-{後}-宮，生壽王淸，諸子莫得爲比，太子浸疎薄。 林甫乃因宦官言-{於}-惠妃，-{願}-盡力保護壽王； 惠妃德之，陰爲内助，由是擢黃門侍郎。 五月，戊子，以裴耀卿爲侍中，張九齡爲中書令，林甫爲禮部尚書、同中書門下三品。
Vice Minister of Personnel Li Linfu was smooth, fawning, and endlessly cunning; he cultivated eunuchs and consorts' kin and watched the Emperor's every move until nothing escaped him. Whenever he memorialized or answered at audience he usually hit the mark, and the Emperor took a liking to him. Consort Wu Huifei then enjoyed favor that eclipsed the entire inner palace; she had borne Prince Shou Li Qing, and no other prince could rival him—the Crown Prince was steadily pushed aside. Linfu then spoke to Huifei through eunuchs, pledging to do everything in his power to protect Prince Shou; Huifei was grateful and quietly backed him from within, and he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat. In the fifth month, on wuzi, Pei Yaoji was appointed Palace Attendant, Zhang Jiuling Grand Councilor, and Linfu Minister of Rites with concurrent status as Grand Councilor.
9
上-{種}-麥-{於}-苑中，帥太子以來親往芟之，謂曰：「此所以-{薦}-宗廟，故不敢不親，且欲使汝曹知稼穡艱難耳。 」又遍以賜侍臣曰：「比遣人視田中稼，多不得實，故自-{種}-以觀之。 」
The Emperor planted wheat in the imperial park, brought the Crown Prince and his brothers to reap it in person, and told them: "This grain is for the ancestral temple, so I dare not leave the work to others—and I want you to understand how hard farming truly is. " He also shared the harvest with his attending ministers, saying: "When I lately sent men to inspect the crops, their reports were often false, so I planted this myself to see the truth. "
10
六月，壬辰，幽州節度使張守珪大破契丹，遣使獻捷。
In the sixth month, on renchen, Youzhou commissioner Zhang Shougui routed the Khitan and sent envoys to report his victory.
11
薛王業疾病，上憂之，容-{發}-爲變。 七月，己巳，薨，贈謚惠宣太子。
Prince Xue Li Ye fell gravely ill; the Emperor was deeply worried, and his face showed it. In the seventh month, on jisi, he died and was posthumously honored as Prince Hui Xuan.
12
上以裴耀卿爲江淮、河南轉運使，-{於}-河口置輸塲。 八月，壬寅，-{於}-輸塲東置河陰倉，西置柏崖倉，三門東置集津倉，西置鹽倉； 鑿漕渠十八-{里}-，以避三門之險。
The Emperor made Pei Yaoji transport commissioner for the Jiang-Huai and Henan regions and established a transshipment depot at the river mouth. In the eighth month, on renyin, east of the depot he built Heyin Granary and west of it Baiya Granary; east of Sanmen Pass he built Jijin Granary and west of it Yan Granary; and he cut an eighteen-li canal to bypass the hazards of Sanmen Pass.
13
先是，舟運江、淮之米至東都含嘉倉，僦車陸運，三百-{里}-至陝，率兩斛用十錢。 耀卿令江、淮舟運悉輸河陰倉，更用河舟運至含嘉倉及太原倉，自太原倉入渭輸關中，凡三歳，運米七百萬斛，省僦車錢三十萬緡。 或説耀卿獻所省錢，耀卿曰：「此公家贏縮之利耳，奈何以之市寵乎！ 」悉奏以爲市糴錢。
Previously, Jiang-Huai grain was shipped by boat to Hejia Granary at Luoyang, then hired carts carried it three hundred li overland to Shan, at a cost of ten cash per two hu. Yaoji required all Jiang-Huai shipping to unload at Heyin Granary, then river boats carried the grain to Hejia and Taiyuan granaries; from Taiyuan it entered the Wei and reached Guanzhong. In three years he moved seven million hu of rice and saved three hundred thousand strings in cart hire. Someone urged Yaoji to present the savings to the throne; he replied: "That is simply the state's operating surplus—how could I trade it for personal favor! " He reported the full amount for use as grain-purchase funds.
14
張果固請歸恆山，-{制}-以爲銀靑光祿大夫，號通玄先生，厚賜而遣之。 -{後}-卒，好異者奏以爲屍解； 上由是頗信神仙。
Zhang Guo insisted on returning to Mount Heng; the Emperor made him Silver-Green Glory Grand Master, styled him Master Tongxuan, gave him lavish gifts, and sent him home. He died later, and enthusiasts of the occult reported that he had achieved corpse liberation; and the Emperor came to believe rather strongly in immortals.
15
冬，十二月，戊子朔，日有食之。
In winter, the twelfth month, on the wuzi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
16
乙巳，幽州節度使張守珪斬契丹王屈烈及可突-{干}-，傳首。 時可突-{干}-連年爲邊患，趙含章、薛楚玉皆不能討。 守珪到官，屢撃破之。 可突-{干}-困迫，遣使詐降，守珪使管記王悔就撫之。 悔至其牙帳，察契丹上下初無降意，但稍徙營帳近西北，密遣人引突厥，謀殺悔以叛； 悔知之。 牙官李過折與可突-{干}-分典兵馬，爭權不-{葉}-，悔説過折使圖之。 過折夜勒兵斬屈烈及可突-{干}-，盡誅其黨，帥-{餘}-衆來降。 守珪出師紫蒙州，大閲以鎭撫之，梟屈烈、可突-{干}-首-{於}-天津之南。
On yisi, Youzhou commissioner Zhang Shougui beheaded the Khitan king Qu Lie and Ketuhan and sent their heads to court. Ketuhan had plagued the frontier for years, and neither Zhao Hanzhang nor Xue Chuyu had been able to defeat him. After Shougui took office he defeated Ketuhan again and again. Hard pressed, Ketuhan sent envoys feigning surrender; Shougui sent his registrar Wang Hui to accept the submission. At the Khitan royal camp Hui saw that they had no real intent to submit, but were merely shifting camps toward the northwest while secretly summoning the Turks and plotting to kill him and rebel; Hui learned of the plot. The yabgu officer Li Guozhe and Ketuhan each commanded troops and were locked in a power struggle; Hui persuaded Guozhe to move against Ketuhan. Guozhe led his troops by night, beheaded Qu Lie and Ketuhan, wiped out their faction, and brought the survivors to surrender. Shougui marched from Zimeng Prefecture, held a grand review to reassure the tribes, and displayed the heads of Qu Lie and Ketuhan south of Tianjin.
17
突厥毘伽可汗爲其大臣梅録啜所毒，未死，討誅梅録啜及其族黨。 既卒，子伊然可汗立。 尋卒，弟登利可汗立。 庚戌，來告喪。 禁京城丐者，置病坊以廩之。
The Turkic Bilge Qaghan was poisoned by his minister Meiluo Chuo; before he died he executed Meiluo Chuo and his entire clan. After his death his son Yiran Qaghan succeeded him. He soon died as well, and his younger brother Dengli Qaghan took the throne. On gengxu envoys arrived to announce the deaths. Begging in the capital was banned, and sick wards were established to feed the destitute.
18
春，正月，契丹知兵馬中郎李過折來獻捷； -{制}-以過折爲北平王，檢校-{松}-漠州都督。
In spring, the first month, the Khitan director of military affairs Li Guozhe came to court with news of victory; and by imperial order he was made Prince of Beiping and acting military governor of Songmo Prefecture.
19
乙亥，上耕藉田，九推乃止； 公卿以下皆終畝。 赦天下，都城酺三日。
On yihai the Emperor plowed the sacred field and stopped after nine turns of the plow; the dukes, ministers, and officials below them each finished an acre. A general amnesty was proclaimed, and the capital feasted for three days.
20
上-{御}-五鳳樓酺宴，觀者喧隘，樂不得奏，金吾白梃如雨，不能遏； 上患之。 髙力士奏河南丞嚴安之爲理嚴，爲人所畏，請使止之； 上從之。 安之至，以手板繞塲畫地曰：「犯此者死！ 」-{於}-是盡三日，人指其畫以相戒，無敢犯者。 時命三百-{里}-内刺史、縣令各帥所部音樂集-{於}-樓下，各較勝負。 懷州刺史上車載樂工數百，皆衣文繡，服箱之牛皆爲虎豹犀象之狀。 魯山令元德秀惟遣樂工數人，連袂歌《-{於}-□》。 上曰：「懷州之人，其塗炭乎！ 」立以刺史爲散官。 德秀性介潔質-{樸}-，士大夫皆服其髙。
The Emperor held the feast at the Five Phoenixes Tower, but the crowd was so dense and unruly that the music could not be played; the Golden Guard beat the mob with white clubs until they rained down, yet still could not restore order; and the Emperor was deeply troubled. Gao Lishi reported that Henan Assistant Magistrate Yan Anzhi was famously stern and feared, and asked that he be sent to restore order; The Emperor agreed. When Anzhi arrived he drew a line around the grounds with his command tablet and declared: "Whoever crosses this line dies! " For the full three days people pointed to his line to warn one another, and no one dared cross it. Prefects and magistrates within three hundred li had each been ordered to bring their local musicians to the tower and compete. The prefect of Huaizhou arrived in a carriage with several hundred musicians, all in brocade, while the oxen pulling the instrument cases were caparisoned as tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, and elephants. The magistrate of Lushan, Yuan Dexiu, sent only a few musicians who stood arm in arm and sang "Yuwei." The Emperor said: "Are the people of Huaizhou being ground to ashes! " He immediately demoted the prefect to an honorary post. Dexiu was upright, scrupulous, and plain in character, and the scholar-official class admired his integrity.
21
上美張守珪之功，欲以爲相，張九齡諫曰：「宰相者，代天理物，非賞功之官也。 」上曰：「假以其名而不使任其職，可乎？ 」對曰：「不可。 惟名與器不可以假人，君之所司也。 且守珪-{才}-破契丹，陛下即以爲宰相； 若盡滅奚、厥，將以何官賞之？ 」上乃止。 二月，守珪詣東都獻捷，拜右羽林大將軍，兼-{御}-史大夫，賜二子官，賞賚甚厚。
Admiring Zhang Shougui's victories, the Emperor wished to make him chancellor; Zhang Jiuling objected: "The chancellor assists Heaven in ordering the realm—it is not a reward for battlefield merit. " The Emperor asked: "Could we give him the title without the duties—would that do? " Jiuling answered: "No. Titles and regalia must never be lent out—that is the ruler's charge alone. Shougui has only just defeated the Khitan, and Your Majesty would already make him chancellor; if he next destroys the Xi and Jue tribes, what office will be left to reward him? " The Emperor abandoned the idea. In the second month Shougui came to Luoyang to present his victory, was made General of the Right Feathered Forest Guard and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, had offices granted to two sons, and received lavish rewards.
22
初，殿中侍-{御}-史楊汪既殺張審素，更名萬頃。 審素二子□、琇皆幼，坐流嶺表； 尋逃歸，謀伺便-{復}-仇。 三月，丁卯，手殺萬頃-{於}-都城。 -{系}-表-{於}-斧，言父冤狀，欲之江外殺與萬頃同謀陷其父者。 至汜水，爲有司所得。 議者多言二子父死非罪，稚年孝烈，能-{復}-父仇，宜加矜宥； 張九齡亦欲活之。 裴耀卿、李林甫以爲如此壞國法，上亦以爲然，謂九齡曰：「孝子之情，義不顧死； 然殺人而赦之，此塗不可啓也。 」乃下敕曰：「國家設法，期-{於}-止殺。 各伸爲子之-{志}-，誰非徇孝之人？ 展轉相仇，何有限極！ 咎繇作士，法在必行。 曾參殺人，亦不可恕。 宜付河南府杖殺。 」士民皆憐之，爲作哀誄，榜-{於}-衢路。 市人斂錢葬之-{於}-北邙。 恐萬頃家-{發}-之，仍爲作疑塚凡數處。
Earlier, Palace Disciplinarian Yang Wang had killed Zhang Shensi and changed his name to Wanqing. Shensi's two young sons, [name missing] and Xiu, were exiled to Lingnan; they soon escaped and plotted to seize a chance for revenge. In the third month, on dingmao, they killed Wanqing with their own hands in the capital. They tied a petition to an axe describing their father's wrongful death and set out to kill, beyond the river, those who had conspired with Wanqing to frame him. At Sishui they were seized by the authorities. Many argued that their father had died innocent, that the boys, young and fiercely filial, had avenged him, and deserved mercy; Zhang Jiuling too wished to spare them. Pei Yaoji and Li Linfu held that this would destroy the law; the Emperor agreed and told Jiuling: "A filial son's passion knows no regard for death; but to kill a man and then pardon the killer— that path must never be opened. " He then issued an edict: "The state establishes laws to end killing. Every man would act as a son—who is not moved by filial duty? Yet if revenge passes back and forth forever, where will it end? When Gao Yao made the Minister of Crime, he meant that law, once proclaimed, must be enforced. Even if the killer were Zeng Shen himself, he could not be forgiven. They are to be handed over to Henan Prefecture to be beaten to death. Scholars and townspeople alike pitied them, wrote elegies in their memory, and posted them at the crossroads. Shopkeepers and townsfolk pooled money to bury them on Mount Beimang north of the capital. Fearing the Wanqing family would exhume the bodies, they also raised several false graves in different spots.
23
唐初，公主實封止三百戸，中宗時，太平公主至五千戸，率以七丁爲限。 開元以來，皇妹止千戸，皇女又半之，皆以三丁爲限； 駙馬皆除三品員外官，而不任以職事。 公主邑入少，至不能具車服，左右或言其太薄，上曰：「百姓租賦，非我所有。 戰士出死力，賞不過束帛； 女子何功，而享多戸邪？ 且欲使之知儉嗇耳。 」秋，七月，-{咸}-宜公主將下嫁，始加實封至千戸。 公主，武惠妃之女也。 -{於}-是諸公主皆加至千戸。
Early in the Tang, a princess's substantive fief was capped at three hundred households; under Emperor Zhongzong, Princess Taiping held as many as five thousand, with a general levy of seven adult males per household. Since the Kaiyuan reign, an emperor's younger sister received no more than one thousand households and an emperor's daughter half that, each household supplying no more than three adult males; Imperial sons-in-law were all granted nominal third-rank supernumerary titles but given no real responsibilities. Princesses' fief income was so slight that some could not even afford full carriages and ceremonial dress, and attendants sometimes complained the allotments were too thin. The Emperor said, "The people's rent and grain are not my private property. Fighting men who stake their lives earn rewards no greater than bundles of silk; what merit have women earned, that they should enjoy so many households? Besides, I mean them to learn thrift." In the seventh month of autumn, as Princess Xianyi was about to marry, her substantive fief was for the first time raised to one thousand households. The princess was a daughter of Consort Wu Hui. Thereupon every princess received an increase to one thousand households.
24
冬，十月，戊申，突騎施寇北庭及安西拔換城。
In winter, the tenth month, on the day wushen, the Turgesh attacked Beiting and Bahuan city in the Anxi protectorate.
25
閏月，壬午朔，日有食之。
In the intercalary month, on the new moon of renyin, the sun was eclipsed.
26
十二月，乙亥，冊故蜀州司戸楊玄琰女爲壽王妃。 玄琰，汪之曾孫也。 是歳，契丹王過折爲其臣涅禮所殺，-{並}-其諸子，一子刺-{乾}-奔安東得免。 涅禮上言，過折用刑殘虐，衆情不安，故殺之。 上赦其罪，因以涅禮爲-{松}-漠都督，且賜書責之曰：「卿之蕃法多無義-{於}-君長，自昔如此，朕亦知之。 然過折是卿之王，有惡輒殺之，爲此王者，不亦難乎！ 但恐卿今爲王，-{後}-人亦爾。 常不自保，誰-{願}-作王！ 亦應防慮-{後}-事，豈得取快目前！ 」突厥尋引兵東侵奚、契丹，涅禮與奚王李歸國共撃破之。
In the twelfth month, on the day yihai, the daughter of the late Yang Xuanyan, registrar of Shuzhou, was invested as consort to the Prince of Shou. Xuanyan was a great-grandson of Yang Wang. That year the Khitan king Guozhe was killed by his minister Nieli, who slew all his sons as well; one son, Cigan, fled to Andong and survived. Nieli reported that Guozhe's punishments had been cruel and brutal, the people were uneasy, and for that reason he had killed him. The Emperor pardoned the crime and appointed Nieli military governor of Songmo, but also sent a letter rebuking him: "Your tribal customs often show little loyalty to lords and elders; that has long been so, and I know it. Yet Guozhe was your king; whenever you found fault you killed him—how hard must it be to be such a king! I only fear that now you are king, those who follow will treat you the same way. If a man cannot even keep himself safe, who would wish to be king! You ought to guard against what comes afterward; how can you satisfy yourself only for the moment!" Soon afterward the Turks led troops east against the Xi and Khitan; Nieli and the Xi king Li Guiguo joined forces and routed them.
27
春，正月，庚寅，敕：「天下逃戸，-{聽}-盡今年内自首，有舊産者令還本貫，無者別俟進止； 逾限不首，當命專使搜求，散配諸軍。 」
In spring, the first month, on the day gengyin, an edict declared: "Fugitive households throughout the realm may surrender themselves before the year's end; those who once held property shall return to their original registers, and those without shall await further orders; whoever fails to surrender after the deadline shall be hunted by special commissioners and assigned scattered among the armies. "
28
北庭都護蓋嘉運撃突騎施，大破之。
Gai Jiayun, protector-general of Beiting, attacked the Turgesh and won a crushing victory.
29
二月，甲寅，宴新除縣令-{於}-朝堂，上作《令長新戒》一篇，賜天下縣令。
In the second month, on the day jiayin, the Emperor feasted newly appointed county magistrates in the audience hall, composed "New Admonitions for Magistrates," and distributed it to every county magistrate in the realm.
30

Under the old system, an assistant director in the Bureau of Appointments supervised the civil examinations. When the presented scholar Li Quan insulted Assistant Director Li Ang, critics argued that the post was too low in rank to command respect from the candidates; in the third month, on the day renchen, an edict ordered that henceforth the vice minister of rites would conduct the civil examinations.

張守珪使平盧討撃使、左驍衞將軍安祿山討奚、契丹叛者，祿山恃勇輕進，爲虜所敗。 夏，四月，辛亥，守珪奏請斬之。 祿山臨刑呼曰：「大夫不欲滅奚、契丹邪！ 奈何殺祿山！ 」守珪亦惜其驍勇，欲活之，乃更執送京師。 張九齡批曰：「昔穰苴誅莊賈，孫武斬宮嬪。 守珪軍令若行，祿山不宜免死。 」上惜其-{才}-，敕令免官，以白衣將領。 九齡固爭曰：「祿山失律喪師，-{於}-法不可不誅。 且臣觀其貌有反相，不殺必爲-{後}-患。 」上曰：「卿勿以王夷甫識石勒，枉害忠良。 」竟赦之。
Zhang Shougui sent the Pinglu campaign commissioner and Left Brave Guards general An Lushan against Xi and Khitan rebels; Lushan, trusting his own bravery, pressed ahead recklessly and was beaten by the enemy. In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinhai, Shougui memorialized asking that Lushan be executed. As the execution neared, Lushan cried out, "My lord, do you not wish to destroy the Xi and Khitan! Why then kill Lushan! Shougui too valued his fighting spirit and wished to spare him, so he had him bound once more and sent to the capital. Zhang Jiuling wrote in his endorsement: "Long ago Rang Ju executed Zhuang Jia, and Sun Wu beheaded the palace women. If Shougui's military law were enforced, Lushan ought not to escape death." The Emperor prized his ability, ordered him stripped of office, and kept him on as a general in plain dress. Jiuling pressed his case: "Lushan broke military law and lost his force; by law he cannot go unpunished. Moreover, I see in his face the look of a rebel; if he is not killed he will surely become a scourge later." The Emperor said, "Do not, like Wang Yifu when he recognized Shi Le, wrongly destroy a loyal man. In the end he pardoned him.

安祿山者，本營州雜胡，初名阿犖山。 其母，巫也； 父死，母攜之再-{適}-突厥安延偃。 會其部落破散，與延偃兄子思順倶逃來，故冒姓安氏，名祿山。 又有史窣-{干}-者，與祿山同裡閉，先-{後}-一日生。 及長，相親愛，皆爲互市牙郎，以驍勇聞。 張守珪以祿山爲捉生將，祿山毎與數騎出，輒擒契丹數十人而返。 狡黠，善揣人情，守珪愛之，養以爲子。
An Lushan was originally a mixed foreigner of Yingzhou and had first been named Aluoshan. His mother was a shaman; after his father died his mother took him and remarried the Turk An Yanyan. When their tribe was shattered, he fled with Yanyan's nephew An Sishun and therefore took the surname An and the name Lushan. There was also a man named Shi Suogan, born in the same neighborhood as Lushan a day apart. When they grew up they were close friends; both became brokers in the border markets and were known for their fighting prowess. Zhang Shougui made Lushan a captive-taking officer; whenever Lushan rode out with a few horsemen he would seize dozens of Khitan and return. Cunning and skilled at reading men, Shougui favored him and raised him as a son.

窣-{干}-嘗負官債亡入奚中，爲奚-{游}-弈所得，欲殺之； 窣-{干}-紿曰：「我，唐之和親使也。 汝殺我，禍且及汝國。 」-{游}-弈信之，送詣牙帳。 窣-{干}-見奚王，長揖不拜，奚王雖怒，而畏唐，不敢殺，以客禮館之，使百人隨窣-{干}-入朝。 窣-{干}-謂奚王曰：「王所遣人雖多，觀其-{才}-皆不足以見天子。 聞王有良將瑣髙者，何不使之入朝！ 」奚王即命瑣髙與牙下三百人隨窣-{干}-入朝。 窣-{干}-將至平盧，先使人謂軍使裴休子曰：「奚使瑣髙與精鋭倶來，聲-{雲}-入朝，實欲襲軍城，宜謹爲之備，先事圖之。 」休子乃具軍容出迎，至館，悉坑殺其從兵，執瑣髙送幽州。 張守珪以窣-{干}-爲有功，奏爲果毅，累遷將軍。 -{後}-入奏事，上與語，悅之，賜名思明。
Suogan once fled into Xi territory to escape an official debt; a Xi patrol seized him and meant to kill him; Suogan deceived them, saying, "I am Tang's marriage envoy. If you kill me, disaster will reach your state as well. The patrol believed him and sent him to the royal tent. When Suogan met the Xi king he bowed from the waist but would not kowtow; though the king was angry, he feared Tang and did not dare kill him, housed him as a guest, and sent a hundred men to follow Suogan to court. Suogan told the Xi king, "Though you send many men, none of them has talent enough to see the Son of Heaven. I hear you have a fine general named Suogao—why not send him to court!" The Xi king at once ordered Suogao and three hundred warriors under his command to follow Suogan to court. Before reaching Pinglu, Suogan sent word to the army commissioner Pei Xiuzi: "The Xi envoy Suogao is coming with picked troops; though they claim to be entering court, they truly mean to strike the garrison—you must prepare carefully and strike first." Xiuzi arrayed his troops and went out to receive them; at the lodge he slaughtered all the followers and sent Suogao captive to Youzhou. Zhang Shougui, crediting Suogan with merit, memorialized to appoint him a guoyi officer, and he rose through the ranks to general. Later, when he came to report at court, the Emperor spoke with him, was pleased, and bestowed the name Siming.

故連州司馬武攸望之子温愼，坐交通權貴，杖死。 乙-{丑}-，朔方、河東節度使信安王禕貶衢州刺史，廣武王承宏貶房州別駕，涇州刺史薛自勸貶澧州別駕； 皆坐與温愼交-{遊}-故也。 承宏，守禮之子也。 辛未，蒲州刺史王琚貶通州刺史； 坐禕交書也。
Wen Shen, son of the former Lianzhou aide Wu Youwang, was punished for trafficking with powerful nobles and beaten to death. On the day yichou, Xin'an Prince Li Yi, military governor of Shuofang and Hedong, was demoted to prefect of Quzhou; Prince of Guangwu Li Chenghong was demoted to assistant prefect of Fangzhou; and Xue Ziqin, prefect of Jingzhou, was demoted to assistant prefect of Lizhou; all for having associated with Wen Shen. Chenghong was a son of Li Shouli. On the day xinwei, Wang Ju, prefect of Pu, was demoted to prefect of Tongzhou; for having exchanged letters with Li Yi.

In the fifth month the sorcerer Liu Zhicheng of Liquan raised a disturbance, driving and plundering travelers as he marched toward Xianyang. 兵部侍郎張均、職方郎中韋述議曰：「聖人知孝人之情深而物類之無限，故爲之節-{制}-。 人之嗜好本無憑準，宴私之饌與時遷移，故聖人一切同歸-{於}-古。 屈到嗜芰，屈建不以-{薦}-，以爲不以私慾-{干}-國之典。 今欲取甘旨肥濃，皆充祭用，苟逾舊-{制}-，其何限焉！ 《書》曰：『黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。 』若以今之珍饌，平生所習，求神無方，何必泥古，則簠簋可去而盤盂杯案當在-{御}-矣，韶濩可息而箜篌箏笛當在奏矣。 既非正物，-{後}-嗣何觀！ 夫神，以精明臨人者也，不求-{豐}-大； 苟失-{於}-禮，雖多何爲！ 豈可廢棄禮經以從流俗！ 且君子愛人以禮，不求苟合； 況在宗廟，敢忘舊章？ 」
Vice Minister of War Zhang Jun and Director of Posts Wei Shu argued: "The sages knew that a filial son's devotion runs deep while the kinds of offerings are limitless, and therefore set regulations. Human taste has no fixed standard; foods for private feasts change with the age, and therefore the sages made all offerings conform to ancient practice. Qu Dao loved water chestnuts, but Qu Jian would not offer them in sacrifice, holding that private appetite must not disturb the state's canonical rites. If every sweet delicacy and rich savory is to be pressed into sacrificial use, and the old regulation is exceeded, where would the limit lie! The Documents says, "It is not millet and sacrificial grain that are fragrant; bright virtue alone is fragrant." If today's delicacies and one's lifelong habits are enough, and in seeking the spirits there is no fixed method and no need to cling to antiquity, then the grain vessels could be discarded and platters, cups, and trays set out instead; the Shao and Hu could fall silent while konghou, zheng, and flutes took their place. Since these are not the proper things, what would later generations behold! The spirits oversee men through keen insight; they do not seek abundance and grandeur; if the rites are lost, what good is abundance! How can one abandon the ritual classics to follow passing fashion! Moreover, the gentleman loves others through ritual and does not seek careless compliance; how much less in the ancestral temple—who would dare forget the old statutes?" "
40
太子賓客崔沔議曰：「祭祀之興，肇-{於}-太古。 茹毛飲血，則有毛血之-{薦}-； 未有-{麴}-薛，則有玄酒之奠。 施及-{後}-王，禮物漸備； 然以神道致敬，不敢廢也。 籩豆簠簋樽罍之實，皆周人之時饌也，其用通-{於}-宴饗賓客，而周公-{制}-禮，與毛血玄酒同-{薦}-鬼神。 國家由禮立訓，因時-{制}--{范}-，淸廟時饗，禮饌必陳，用周-{制}-也。 園寢上食，時膳具設，遵漢法也。 職貢來祭，致遠物也。 有新必-{薦}-，順時令也。 苑囿之内，躬稼所收，搜狩之時，親-{發}-所中，莫不-{薦}-而-{後}-食，盡誠敬也。 若此至矣，-{復}-何加焉！ 但當申敕有司，無或簡怠，則鮮美肥濃，盡在是矣，不必加籩豆之數也。 」
Cui Hao, guest of the heir apparent, argued: "Sacrifice arose in utmost antiquity. When men ate raw flesh and drank blood, there were offerings of fur and blood; before there was leavened grain and yeast, there was the offering of dark wine. Under later kings ritual objects gradually became complete; yet in reverence to the spirits they did not dare abolish the older offerings. The contents of baskets, stands, grain vessels, and wine jars were foods of Zhou times, used alike at feasts and for entertaining guests, yet the Duke of Zhou established ritual and offered them to the spirits together with fur, blood, and dark wine. The state establishes instruction through ritual and shapes regulations and standards to the times; at seasonal offerings in the Pure Temple, ritual foods must be set out—this follows Zhou practice. At the park-tombs the presentation of food, with seasonal viands fully set out, follows Han practice. When tribute offices come to sacrifice, they present goods brought from afar. Whenever there is something new it must be offered—that is observing the seasons. Within the imperial parks, grain from the Emperor's own plowing and game from his own bow at the hunt were all offered before being eaten—such was the fullness of sincerity and reverence. When devotion has reached this point, what more could be added! The responsible offices need only be charged sternly not to be remiss or negligent; then every fresh delicacy and rich savory will be fully provided—there is no need to increase the number of baskets and stands. "

縚又奏：「《喪服》『舅，緦麻三月，從母，外祖父母皆小功五月。 』外祖至尊，同-{於}-從母之服； 姨、舅一等，服則輕重有殊。 堂姨、舅親即未疎，恩絶不相爲服，舅母來承外族，不如同爨之禮。 竊以古意猶有所未暢者也，請加外祖父母爲大功九月，姨、舅皆小功五月，堂舅、堂姨、舅母-{並}-加至袒免。 」
Wei Tao again memorialized: "The Mourning Garments states, "For an uncle, sizang mourning for three months; for a mother's sister and for maternal grandparents, xiaogong mourning for five months. " The maternal grandfather, though supremely honored, wears the same mourning as a mother's sister; yet aunt and uncle are of one rank while their mourning garments differ in weight. Paternal cousins among aunts and uncles are not yet distant in kinship, yet no mourning is worn for one another; an uncle's wife, joining the outer clan, is treated less favorably than those who shared the same hearth. I venture to think the ancient meaning still has points not fully expressed; I request that maternal grandparents be raised to dagong mourning for nine months, that aunts and uncles all receive xiaogong mourning for five months, and that paternal uncles, paternal aunts, and uncles' wives all be raised to taboo mourning. "

崔沔議曰：「正家之道，不可以貳； 總一定義，理歸本宗。 是以内有齊、斬，外皆緦麻，尊名所加，不過一等，此先王不易之道也。 -{願}-守八年明旨，一依古禮，以爲萬代成法。 」
Cui Mian argued: "The way to set the household in order cannot be twofold; when principle is gathered into one fixed meaning, reason returns to the main lineage. Therefore within the family there are qi and zhan mourning, while without all is sizang; where honor adds to a name, it does not exceed one grade—this is the unchanging way of the former kings. I wish to uphold the clear decree of the eighth year and follow the ancient rites alone, making them the established law for ten thousand generations." "

韋述議曰：「《喪服傳》曰：『禽獸知母而不知父。 野人曰，父母何等焉！ 都邑之士則知尊檷矣； 大夫及學士則知尊祖矣。 』聖人究天道而厚-{於}-祖檷，-{系}-族姓而親其子孫，母黨比-{於}-本族，不可同貫，明矣。 今若外祖及舅加服一等，堂舅及姨列-{於}-服紀，則中外之-{制}-，相去-{幾}-何！ 廢禮徇情，所務者末。 古之-{製}-作者，知人情之易搖，恐失禮之將漸，別其同異，輕重相懸，欲使-{後}-來之人永不相雜。 微旨斯在，豈徒然哉！ 苟可加也，亦可減也； 往聖可得而非，則《禮經》可得而隳矣。 先王之-{制}-，謂之彝倫，奉以周旋，猶恐失墜； 一紊其敘，庸可止乎！ 請依《儀禮》喪服爲定。 」
Wei Shu argued: "The Commentary on Mourning Garments says, "Beasts know their mother but not their father. The rustic says, How can father and mother be equal! The townsman of the capital knows how to honor his father; the grandee and the scholar know how to honor their ancestors. " The sage exhausts the way of Heaven and is deep toward ancestors and father; he ties clan surnames and cherishes their descendants—the mother's kin compared with the main clan cannot be treated as one thread; this is clear. If now maternal grandparents and uncles have their mourning raised one grade, and paternal uncles and aunts are entered in the mourning registers, how far apart would the regulations for inner and outer kin remain! To abandon ritual and indulge feeling is to pursue what is peripheral. The makers of old knew how easily human feeling sways and feared that ritual would slip away by degrees; they distinguished sameness from difference and set light and heavy far apart, wishing that later generations would never mix the two. The subtle purpose lies here—how could it be in vain! If mourning may be increased, it may also be reduced; if the sages of old may be faulted, then the Book of Rites may be overthrown. The regulations of the former kings are called the constant norms; in observing them through every turn one still fears they may be lost; once their order is thrown into confusion, how can it be stopped! I request that the mourning garments of the Ceremonies and Rites be taken as fixed." "

Yang Zhongchang, vice director in the Ministry of Rites, argued: "Duke Wen Zhen Wei Zheng was the first to raise mourning for an uncle to xiaogong for five months. Though Wen Zhen was worthy, the Duke of Zhou and Confucius were sages; to let a worthy man alter the sages—what are later students to follow! I fear that inner and outer kin would fall out of order and near and distant would usurp one another's stations; where feeling leads, what would not be reached! Formerly Zilu was in mourning for a sister but did not lay it aside; Confucius said, "The former kings made ritual; even men who walk the Way cannot bear it. " Zilu laid the mourning aside. This is a clear example of how the sage, drawing on the matter at hand, restrained feeling. The Record says, "Do not lightly discuss ritual. " This shows that it coils through Heaven and Earth and ranks with sun and moon; the worthy follow it—how would one dare to add or subtract!" "

In autumn, the eighth month, on renzi, the Thousand Autumns Festival; all the ministers presented precious mirrors. Zhang Jiuling held that a mirror shows one's own form while other men reveal fortune and misfortune; he therefore set forth the sources of rise and fall in former ages, compiled a book in five scrolls called Records of the Thousand Autumns Golden Mirror, and presented it; The Emperor bestowed a written commendation in praise.

On yihai, Prince Ai of Bian, Li Jin, died.

冬，十月，戊申，車駕-{發}-東都。 先是，敕以來年二月二日行幸西京，會宮中有怪，明日，上召宰相，即議西還。 裴耀卿、張九齡曰：「今農收未畢，請俟仲冬。 」李林甫潛知上指，二相退，林甫獨留，言-{於}-上曰：「長安、洛陽，陛下東西宮耳，往來行幸，何更擇時！ 借使妨-{於}-農收，但應蠲所過租稅而已。 臣請宣示百司，即日西行。 」上悅，從之。 過陝州，以刺史盧奐有善政，題贊-{於}-其-{聽}-事而去。 奐，懷愼之子也。 丁卯，至西京。 朔方節度使牛仙客，前在河西，能節用度，勤職業，倉庫充實，器械精利； 上聞而嘉之，欲加尚書。 張九齡曰：「不可。 尚書，古之納言，唐興以來，惟舊相及揚歴中外有德望者乃爲之。 仙客本河湟使典，今驟居淸要，恐羞朝廷。 」上曰：「然則但加實封可乎？ 」對曰：「不可。 封爵所以勸有功也。 邊將實倉庫，修器械，乃常務耳，不足爲功。 陛下賞其勤，賜之金帛可也； 裂土封之，恐非其宜。 」上默然。 李林甫言-{於}-上曰：「仙客，宰相-{才}-也，何有-{於}-尚書！ 九齡書生，不達大體。 」上悅。 明日，-{復}-以仙客實封爲言，九齡固執如初。 上怒，變色曰：「事皆由卿邪？ 」九齡頓首謝曰：「陛下不知臣愚，使待罪宰相，事有未允，臣不敢不盡言。 」上曰：「卿嫌仙客寒微，如卿有何閥閲！ 」九齡曰：「臣嶺海孤賤，不如仙客生-{於}-中華； 然臣出入-{台}-閣，典司誥命有年矣。 仙客邊隅小吏，目不知書，若大任之，恐不愜衆望。 」林甫退而言曰：「苟有-{才}-識，何必辭學！ 天子用人，有何不可！ 」十一月，戊戌，賜仙客爵隴西縣公，食實封三百戸。
In winter, the tenth month, on wushen, the imperial carriage set out from Luoyang. Earlier an edict had set the second day of the second month of the coming year for a progress to Chang'an; when strange things occurred in the palace, the next day the Emperor summoned the chief ministers and at once discussed returning west. Pei Yaoji and Zhang Jiuling said, "The harvest is not yet complete; we ask that Your Majesty wait until mid-winter. " Li Linfu secretly knew the Emperor's intent; the two chief ministers withdrew, and Li Linfu alone remained, saying to the Emperor, "Chang'an and Luoyang are merely Your Majesty's eastern and western palaces; in coming and going on progress, why choose the season! Even if it should hinder the harvest, one need only remit rent and tax along the route. Your servant asks that the hundred offices be notified and that the western journey begin this very day. " The Emperor was pleased and followed his advice. Passing through Shazhou, because Prefect Lu Huan had governed well the Emperor inscribed a commendation in his hall of audience and departed. Lu Huan was a son of Lu Huaishen. On dingmao, he arrived at Chang'an. Niu Xianke, military governor of Shuofang, while previously in Hexi had economized expenditures, diligently performed his duties, filled the storehouses, and kept weapons sharp and ready; The Emperor heard of this and commended him, wishing to promote him to Minister. Zhang Jiuling said, "This cannot be done. The Minister was the nayan of old; since the founding of Tang, only former chief ministers and those who had risen through central and provincial service with virtue and reputation held the post. Xianke was originally a clerk in the Hehuang commission; to place him suddenly in a pure and vital post would, I fear, bring shame on the court. " The Emperor said, "Then would it suffice merely to add substantive enfeoffment? " He replied, "This also cannot be done. Titles and enfeoffments exist to encourage those who have merit. For a frontier general to fill storehouses and repair weapons is merely routine duty and does not count as merit. Your Majesty may reward his diligence with gold and silks; to carve out land and enfeoff him—I fear that would not be fitting. " The Emperor fell silent. Li Linfu said to the Emperor, "Xianke has the talent of a chief minister—what is there in the post of Minister! Jiuling is a bookish man who does not grasp the larger pattern. " The Emperor was pleased. The next day the Emperor again spoke of substantive enfeoffment for Xianke; Zhang Jiuling held firm as before. The Emperor grew angry, his countenance changing, and said, "Must all affairs go as you say? " Zhang Jiuling bowed his head and apologized, saying, "Your Majesty did not know my foolishness when you made me serve as chief minister; when a matter is not fitting, your servant dares not fail to speak fully. " The Emperor said, "You despise Xianke as lowborn and humble—what noble lineage have you! " Zhang Jiuling said, "Your servant is a lonely and lowly man of the Lingnan seas and is not the equal of Xianke, born in the central domains; yet your servant has gone in and out of the terrace offices and for years presided over imperial pronouncements. Xianke is a petty clerk of the frontier marches who cannot read; if he were given a great appointment, I fear he would not satisfy public expectation. " After withdrawing, Li Linfu said, "If one has talent and insight, why must one be versed in letters! When the Son of Heaven employs men, what may not be done! " In the eleventh month, on wuxu, Xianke was granted the title Duke of Longxi County with substantive enfeoffment of three hundred households.
53
初，上欲以李林甫爲相，問-{於}-中書令張九齡，九齡對曰：「宰相-{系}-國安危，陛下相林甫，臣恐異日爲廟社之憂。 」上不從。 時九齡方以文學爲上所重，林甫雖恨，猶-{曲}-意事之。 侍中裴耀卿與九齡善，林甫-{並}-疾之。 是時，上在位歳久，漸肆奢欲，怠-{於}-政事。 而九齡遇事無細大皆力爭； 林甫巧伺上意，日思所以中傷之。
Earlier, when the Emperor wished to make Li Linfu chief minister, he asked Secretariat Director Zhang Jiuling; Zhang Jiuling replied, "The chief minister is tied to the state's safety and peril; if Your Majesty makes Li Linfu chief minister, your servant fears that one day he will become a worry for the altars of soil and grain. " The Emperor did not follow his advice. At that time Zhang Jiuling was still highly valued by the Emperor for his literary learning; though Li Linfu hated him, he still bent his will to serve him. Palace Attendant Pei Yaoji was on good terms with Zhang Jiuling, and Li Linfu hated them both. At this time the Emperor had been on the throne many years and gradually gave free rein to luxurious desires and grew slack in government affairs. Zhang Jiuling, meanwhile, strove forcefully over every matter, great or small; Li Linfu cleverly watched the Emperor's intent and daily thought how to wound him.
54
上之爲臨淄王也，趙麗妃、皇甫德儀、劉-{才}-人皆有寵，麗妃生太子瑛，德儀生鄂王瑤，-{才}-人生光王琚。 及即位，幸武惠妃，麗妃等愛皆馳； 惠妃生壽王瑁，寵冠諸子。 太子與瑤、琚會-{於}-内第，各以母失職有怨望語。 駙馬都尉楊洄尚-{咸}-宜公主，常伺三子過失以告惠妃。 惠妃泣訴-{於}-上曰：「太子陰結黨與，將害妾母子，亦指斥至尊。 」上大怒，以語宰相，欲皆廢之。 九齡曰：「陛下踐祚垂三十年，太子諸王不離深宮，日受聖訓，天下之人皆慶陛下享國久長，子孫蕃昌。 今三子皆已成人，不聞大過，陛下奈何一旦以無根之語，喜怒之際，盡廢之乎！ 且太子天下本，不可輕搖。 昔晉獻公-{聽}-驪姬之讒殺申生，三世大亂。 漢武帝信江充之誣罪戾太子，京城流血。 晉惠帝用賈-{後}-之譖廢愍懷太子，中原塗炭。 隋文帝納獨孤-{後}-之言黜太子勇，立煬帝，遂失天下。 由此觀之，不可不愼。 陛下必欲爲此，臣不敢奉詔。 」上不悅。 林甫初無所言，退而私謂宦官之貴幸者曰：「此主上家事，何必問外人！ 」上猶豫未決。 惠妃密使官奴牛貴兒謂九齡曰：「有廢必有興，公爲之援，宰相可長處。 」九齡叱之，以其語白上； 上爲之動色，故訖九齡罷相，太子得無動。 林甫日夜短九齡-{於}-上，上浸疎之。
When the Emperor was Prince of Linzi, Consort Zhao Li, Lady Huangfu De, and Lady Liu Cai all had his favor; Consort Li bore the crown prince Ying, Lady De bore Prince E Yao, and Lady Cai bore Prince Guang Ju. When he took the throne he favored Consort Wu Hui, and the love for Consort Li and the others all ran off; Consort Hui bore Prince Shou Mao, whose favor surpassed all the other sons. The crown prince met with Yao and Ju in the inner quarters, and each spoke resentful words because his mother had lost her position. Commandant of Horse Yang Hui had married Princess Xianyi and constantly watched the three sons' faults to report them to Consort Hui. Consort Wu Hui wept and appealed to the Emperor, saying, "The crown prince is secretly forming a faction and will harm me and my son; he also denounces Your Majesty." " The Emperor was greatly enraged, told the chief ministers, and wished to depose them all. Zhang Jiuling said, "Your Majesty has occupied the throne for nearly thirty years; the crown prince and the princes have not left the inner palace and daily receive your sagely instruction; all under Heaven rejoice that Your Majesty will enjoy the state long and that your sons and grandsons will flourish. Now all three sons are grown men, and no great fault is heard of them—how can Your Majesty, in a moment of anger, on groundless words, depose them all! Moreover, the crown prince is the root of the realm and must not be lightly shaken. Formerly Duke Xian of Jin heeded Lady Li's slander and killed Prince Shensheng, and three generations fell into great disorder. Emperor Wu of Han believed Jiang Chong's false charge against the heir apparent, and blood flowed in the capital. Emperor Hui of Jin took Empress Jia's slander and deposed Crown Prince Minhuai, and the central plains were laid waste. Emperor Wen of Sui accepted Empress Dugu's words, removed Crown Prince Yong, and enthroned Emperor Yang, and thus lost the realm. Viewed from this, one cannot but be careful. If Your Majesty insists on doing this, your servant dares not obey the edict. " The Emperor was displeased. Li Linfu at first said nothing; after withdrawing he privately told a favored eunuch, "This is the sovereign's own family affair—why must outsiders be consulted! " The Emperor hesitated and had not yet decided. Consort Hui secretly sent the official slave Niu Guier to tell Zhang Jiuling, "Where there is deposition there must be elevation; if you lend your support, you may long hold the post of chief minister. " Zhang Jiuling rebuked him and reported his words to the Emperor; the Emperor's expression changed at this, and so until Zhang Jiuling was removed as chief minister the crown prince remained unmoved. Li Linfu day and night spoke ill of Zhang Jiuling to the Emperor, and the Emperor gradually grew distant from him.
55
林甫引蕭炅爲戸部侍郎。 炅素不學，嘗對中書侍郎嚴挺之讀「伏-{臘}-」爲「伏獵」。 挺之言-{於}-九齡曰：「省中豈容有『伏獵侍郎』！ 」由是出炅爲岐州刺史，故林甫怨挺之。 九齡與挺之善，欲引以爲相，嘗謂之曰：「李尚書方承恩，足下宜一造門，與之款暱。 」挺之素負氣，薄林甫爲人，竟不之詣； 林甫恨之益深。 挺之先娶妻，出之，更嫁蔚州刺史王元琰，元琰坐贓罪下三司按鞫，挺之爲之營解。 林甫因左右使-{於}-禁中白上。 上謂宰相曰：「挺之爲罪人請屬所由。 」九齡曰：「此乃挺之出妻，不宜有情。 」上曰：「雖離乃-{復}-有私。 」
Li Linfu brought in Xiao Jiong as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue. Jiong had never studied and once, facing Secretariat Vice Director Yan Tingzhi, read fu-la (winter and summer sacrifices) as fu-lie (crouching to hunt). Tingzhi spoke to Zhang Jiuling, saying, "How can the Secretariat tolerate a 'Crouching Hunt Vice Minister'! " Thereupon Jiong was sent out as prefect of Qizhou, and so Li Linfu resented Tingzhi. Zhang Jiuling was on good terms with Tingzhi and wished to bring him in as chief minister; he once told him, "Minister Li is just now enjoying favor—you should pay one visit to his door and become close with him. " Tingzhi had always been proud of spirit and looked down on Li Linfu's character; in the end he did not go; and Li Linfu hated him all the more deeply. Tingzhi had earlier taken a wife and divorced her; she remarried Wang Yuanyan, prefect of Yu Prefecture. Yuanyan was charged with corruption and sent down to the Three Offices for investigation; Tingzhi worked to secure his release on his behalf. Li Linfu used those close at hand to report this to the Emperor within the palace. The Emperor told the chief ministers, "Tingzhi is pleading on behalf of a criminal with those who handle the case. " Zhang Jiuling said, "This is Tingzhi's divorced wife; he ought not to harbor affection. " The Emperor said, "Though divorced, he still has private feeling. "
56
-{於}-是上積前事，以耀卿、九齡爲阿黨； 壬寅，以耀爲左丞相，九齡爲右丞相，-{並}-罷政事。 以林甫兼中書令； 仙客爲工部尚書、同中書門下三品，鄰朔方節度如故。 嚴挺之貶洺州刺史，王元琰流嶺南。
Thereupon the Emperor piled up earlier matters and treated Yaoji and Jiuling as a clique; on renyin he made Yaoji Left Chief Minister and Jiuling Right Chief Minister, and both were removed from active government. Li Linfu was made concurrent Secretariat Director; Xianke was made Minister of Works and Associate Secretariat Director of the Third Rank, still retaining his Shuofang command as before. Yan Tingzhi was demoted to prefect of Ming Prefecture, and Wang Yuanyan was banished to Lingnan.
57
上即位以來，所用之相，姚崇尚通，宋珪尚法，張嘉貞尚吏，張説尚文，李元紘、杜暹尚儉，韓休、張九齡尚直，各其所長也。 九齡既得罪，自是朝廷之士，皆容身保位，無-{復}-直言。
Since the Emperor took the throne, the chief ministers he had used each had their strength: Yao Chong valued comprehensiveness, Song Jing valued law, Zhang Jiazhen valued administration, Zhang Yue valued letters, Li Yuanhong and Du Xian valued frugality, Han Xiu and Zhang Jiuling valued uprightness—each his own forte. Once Zhang Jiuling had fallen from favor, from then on the men of court all sheltered themselves and guarded their posts, and none again spoke plainly.
58
李林甫欲蔽塞人主視-{聽}-，自專大權，明召諸諫官謂曰：「今明主在上，群臣將順之不暇，烏用多言！ 諸君不見立仗馬乎？ 食三品料，一鳴輒斥去，悔之何及！ 」
Li Linfu wished to block the sovereign lord's sight and hearing and monopolize great power; he openly summoned the remonstrance officials and said, "Now a brilliant sovereign is above; the ministers can scarcely keep pace in yielding to him—what use is much talk! Do you gentlemen not see the horses of the palace guard formation? They eat third-rank rations; one neigh and they are driven away—how can regret come in time! "
59
補闕杜璡嘗上書言事，明日，黜爲下邽令。 自是諫爭路絶矣。
Palace Remonstrator Du Lin once submitted a memorial on state affairs; the next day he was demoted to magistrate of Xiayi. From then on the road of remonstrance and dispute was cut off.
60
牛仙客既爲林甫所引進，專給唯諾而已。 然二人皆謹守格式，百官遷除，各有常度，雖奇-{才}-異行，不免終老常調； 其以巧諂邪險自進者，則超騰不次，自有它蹊矣。 林甫城府深密，人莫窺其際。 好以甘言啖人，而陰中傷之，不露辭色。 凡爲上所厚者，始則親結之，及位勢稍逼，輒以計去之。 雖老-{奸}-巨猾，無能逃其-{術}-者。
Niu Xianke, having been brought in by Li Linfu, did nothing but supply yeses and nos. Yet the two men both strictly observed regulations and forms; promotions and removals of the hundred officials each had their fixed measure, and even men of rare talent and unusual conduct could not escape ending their days in routine appointments; those who advanced by crafty flattery, wickedness, and treachery, however, leaped up out of order and had their own other paths. Li Linfu's mind was a deep and sealed fortress; no one could glimpse its bounds. He liked to feed men with sweet words while secretly striking them down, without revealing it in speech or countenance. All whom the Emperor favored he would at first draw close and bind to himself; once rank and power drew slightly near, he would remove them by stratagem. Even old villains and great rogues could not escape his methods.
61
春，正月，初置玄學博士，毎歳依明經舉。
In spring, the first month, the post of Doctor of the Learning of the Mysterious was first established; each year candidates were raised by the same method as for the Classicist degree.
62
二月，敕曰：「進士以聲韻爲學，多昧古今； 明經以貼誦爲功，罕窮旨趣。 自今明經問大義十條，對時務策三首； 進士試大經十貼。 」
In the second month an edict said, "Jinshi scholars take tonal prosody as their study and are mostly ignorant of past and present; Classicists take pasted recitation as their achievement and rarely penetrate the essential meaning. From now on Classicists shall be questioned on ten items of great principle and answer three policy essays on current affairs; jinshi candidates shall be tested on ten pasted passages from the great classics. "
63
戊辰，新羅王興光卒，子承慶襲位。
On wuchen King Xingguang of Silla died, and his son Chengqing succeeded to the throne.
64
乙酉，幽州節度使張守珪破契丹-{於}-捺祿山。
On yiyou Zhang Shougui, military governor of Youzhou, defeated the Khitan at Nalushan.
65
己亥，河西節度使崔希逸襲吐蕃，破之-{於}-靑海西。
On jihai Cui Xiyi, military governor of Hexi, raided the Tibetans and defeated them west of Qinghai.
66
初，希逸遣使謂吐蕃邊將乞力徐曰：「兩國通好，今爲一家，何必更置兵守捉，妨人耕牧！ 請皆罷之。 」乞力徐曰：「常侍忠厚，言必不欺。 然朝廷未必專以邊事相委，萬一有-{奸}-人交-{斗}-其間，掩吾無備，悔之何及！ 」希逸固請，乃刑白狗爲盟，各去守備； -{於}-是吐蕃畜牧被野。 時吐蕃西撃勃律，勃律來告急。 上命吐蕃罷兵，吐蕃不奉詔，遂破勃律； 上甚怒。 會希逸傔人孫誨入奏事，自欲求功，奏稱吐蕃無備，請掩撃，必大獲。 上命内給事趙惠琮與誨偕往，審察事宜。 惠琮等至，則矯詔令希逸襲之。 希逸不得已，-{發}-兵自涼州南入吐蕃境二千-{餘}--{里}-，至靑海西，與吐蕃戰，大破之，斬首二千-{餘}-級，乞力徐脱身走。 惠琮、誨皆受厚賞。 自是吐蕃-{復}-絶朝貢。
Earlier, Xiyi sent an envoy to tell the Tibetan frontier general Qili Xu, "Our two states are on good terms and are now one family—why must we still post troops to guard and seize, hindering men's plowing and herding! I ask that we all withdraw them. " Qili Xu said, "The Regular Attendant is honest and generous; his words surely will not deceive. Yet the court may not entrust frontier affairs to you alone; should some villain stir strife between us and strike us unprepared, how can regret come in time! " Xiyi pressed his request firmly, and so they slaughtered a white dog to seal the covenant and each withdrew his garrisons; thereupon Tibetan herds and flocks spread across the wild. At that time the Tibetans were striking Bolü in the west, and Bolü came to report urgency. The Emperor ordered the Tibetans to cease military action; the Tibetans did not obey the edict and thereupon destroyed Bolü; the Emperor was greatly angered. It happened that Xiyi's attendant Sun Hui came in to report on affairs; wishing merit for himself, he memorialized that the Tibetans were unprepared and asked for a surprise attack, saying great gains were certain. The Emperor ordered Inner Provisioner Zhao Huizong to go with Hui and examine the matter on the spot. When Huizong and the others arrived, they forged an edict ordering Xiyi to attack. Xiyi had no choice; he raised troops from Liangzhou south into Tibetan territory more than two thousand li, reaching west of Qinghai, fought the Tibetans, and routed them greatly, beheading more than two thousand; Qili Xu escaped and fled. Huizong and Hui both received rich rewards. From then on the Tibetans again cut off court tribute.
67
夏，四月，辛酉，監察-{御}-史周子諒彈牛仙客非-{才}-，引讖書爲證。 上怒，命左右手暴-{於}-殿庭，絶而-{復}-甦； 仍杖之朝堂，流瀼州，至藍田而死。 李林甫言：「子諒，張九齡所-{薦}-也。 」甲子，貶九齡荊州長史。
In summer, the fourth month, on xinyou Supervising Censor Zhou Ziliang impeached Niu Xianke as lacking talent and cited apocryphal texts as proof. The Emperor was enraged and ordered the attendants to beat him bare-handed in the palace courtyard until he ceased breathing and then revived him; he was still caned in the court hall, banished to Rang Prefecture, and died at Lantian on the way. Li Linfu said, "Ziliang was recommended by Zhang Jiuling. " On jiazi Zhang Jiuling was demoted to senior administrator of Jing Prefecture.
68
楊洄又譖太子瑛、鄂王瑤、光王琚，-{雲}-與太子妃兄駙馬薛銹潛構異謀，上召宰相謀之。 李林甫對曰：「此陛下家事，非臣等所宜豫。 」上意乃決。 乙-{丑}-，使宦者宣-{制}--{於}-宮中，廢瑛、瑤、琚爲庶人，流銹-{於}-瀼州。 瑛、瑤、琚尋賜死城東驛，銹賜死-{於}-藍田。 瑤、琚皆好學，有-{才}-識，死不以罪，人皆惜之。 丙寅，瑛舅家趙氏、妃家薛氏、瑤舅家皇甫氏，坐流貶者數十人，惟瑤妃家韋氏以妃賢得免。
Yang Hui again slandered Crown Prince Ying, Prince E Yao, and Prince Guang Ju, saying that with the crown prince's consort's elder brother, Imperial Son-in-law Xue Xiu, they were secretly plotting rebellion; the Emperor summoned the chief ministers to deliberate. Li Linfu replied, "This is Your Majesty's own family affair and is not what your servants ought to take part in. " The Emperor's mind was then decided. On yichou he sent eunuchs to proclaim the edict within the palace, deposed Ying, Yao, and Ju as commoners, and banished Xiu to Rang Prefecture. Ying, Yao, and Ju were soon ordered to die at the eastern post station; Xiu was ordered to die at Lantian. Yao and Ju both loved learning and had talent and insight; they died without guilt, and all regretted it. On bingyin the Zhao clan of Ying's mother's family, the Xue clan of his consort's family, and the Huangfu clan of Yao's mother's family—several tens of persons were implicated and banished; only the Wei clan of Yao's consort's family was spared because the consort was virtuous.

Previously, along the northwest frontier dozens of prefectures had long kept large garrisons; local rents and military farm yields could not sustain them, and the government began buying grain at fair prices to make up the shortfall. After Crown Prince Ying's death, Li Linfu repeatedly urged the Emperor to make Prince Shou Li Mao heir. The Emperor favored Prince of Zhong Li Yu as the eldest son—filial, reverent, studious—and meant to name him heir, yet hesitated for more than a year. He brooded on his advancing age, on three sons executed in a single day, and on an unsettled succession; he grew restless and joyless, and even sleep and appetite failed him. Gao Lishi seized a quiet moment to ask what troubled him. The Emperor said, "You are the old slave of my house—can you not read my mind! Lishi said, "Is it not because the heir is still undecided?" The Emperor said, "Yes." He replied, "Why weary yourself so? Simply install the eldest—who would dare dispute it!" The Emperor said, "You are right!" You are right! And so the matter was settled. In the sixth month, on gengzi, Li Yu was installed as Crown Prince.

The Turgesh khan Suluo was frugal by nature; after every battle he divided the spoils among his tribes and kept nothing for himself, and his people gladly followed him. Though he had married a Tang princess, he also dealt secretly with the Turks and Tibet, and each realm gave him a wife. Suluo took wives from all three powers as khatuns and made several sons yabghus; expenses mounted, and he no longer shared the spoils of war. In his later years he suffered a paralytic stroke; one hand curled useless, and the tribes lost heart. Chiefs Mohedagan and Dumedu were the strongest factions; their people further split into Yellow and Black surnames at odds with one another. Mohedagan then led a night attack on Suluo and killed him. Dumedu had first plotted with Mohedagan, then turned against him; he set up Suluo's son Guchuo as Khan Tuhuoxian to rally the remnants, and the two factions warred on each other. Mohedagan sent envoys to Beiting military governor Gai Jiayun; the Emperor ordered Jiayun to rally Turgesh, Fergana, and the states beyond. Tuhuoxian and Dumedu held Suyab; the Black Surname khan Erwei Tele held Talas; together they raised arms against Tang.

Du Xiwang led the Shazhou army to seize Tibet's river bridge and built Salt Spring Fort on the left bank. Tibet sent thirty thousand men to meet him; Xiwang's force was too small, and his officers and men were afraid. Left Majestic Guard commandant Wang Zhongsi led his men in the first charge; wherever he struck the enemy gave way; he killed several hundred and threw their line into disorder. Xiwang then threw his whole force forward, and the Tibetans were routed. The Zhenxi Army was established at Salt Spring. 歸義之先本哀牢夷，地居姚州之西，東南接交趾，西北接吐蕃。 蠻語謂王曰詔，先有六詔：曰蒙-{捨}-，曰蒙越，曰越析，曰浪穹，曰樣備，曰越澹，兵力相埒，莫能相壹； 歴代因之以分其勢。 蒙-{捨}-最在南，故謂之南詔。 髙宗時，蒙-{捨}-細奴邏初入朝。 細奴邏生邏盛，邏盛生盛邏皮，盛邏皮生皮邏閣。 皮邏閣浸強大，而五詔微弱； 會有破渳河蠻之功，乃賂王昱，求合六詔爲一。 昱爲之奏請，朝遷許之，仍賜名歸義。 -{於}-是以兵威脅服群蠻，不從者滅之，遂撃破吐蕃，徙居大和城； 其-{後}-卒爲邊患。
Guiyi's people were originally Ailao Yi, living west of Yaozhou, with Jiaozhi to the southeast and Tibet to the northwest. In their tongue a king was called zhao. Six zhao had long existed—Mengshe, Mengyue, Yuexi, Langqiong, Yangbei, and Yuetan—each with comparable strength and none able to subdue the rest; successive dynasties had relied on that division to keep them weak. Mengshe lay farthest south, hence the name Nan Zhao, Southern Zhao. In Emperor Gaozong's reign Xinuoluo of Mengshe first came to court. Xinuoluo was succeeded by Luosheng, then Shengluopi, then Piluoge. Piluoge grew steadily stronger while the other five zhao weakened; after defeating the Mishe River tribes he bribed Wang Yu to petition that the six zhao be united under one rule. Wang Yu memorialized on his behalf; the court agreed and bestowed the name Guiyi. Thereafter he cowed the other tribes by force, destroyed those who refused submission, defeated Tibet, and moved his seat to Dali; and in time he became a scourge on the frontier.

In the sixth month, on guiyou Censor-in-Chief Li Shizhi was also made military governor of Youzhou.
110
幽州將趙堪、白眞阤羅矯節度使張守珪之命，使平盧軍使烏知義邀撃叛奚-{餘}-黨-{於}-橫水之北； 知義不從，白眞阤羅矯稱-{制}-指以迫之。 知義不得已出師，與虜遇，先勝-{後}-敗； 守珪隱其敗狀，以克獲聞。 事頗洩，上令内謁者監牛仙童作察之。 守珪重賂仙童，歸罪-{於}-白眞阤羅，逼令自縊死。 仙童有寵-{於}-上，衆宦官疾之，共-{發}-其事。 上怒，甲戌，命楊思勗杖殺之。 思勗縛格，杖之數百，刳取其心，割其肉啖之。 守珪坐貶括州刺史。 太子太師蕭-{嵩}-嘗賂仙童以城南良田數頃，李林甫-{發}-之，-{嵩}-坐貶靑州刺史。
Youzhou generals Zhao Kan and Bai Zhentuoluo forged orders in Zhang Shougui's name directing Pinglu commander Wu Zhiyi to strike remnant Xi rebels north of Hengshui; Zhiyi refused; Bai Zhentuoluo then forged an imperial directive to force him out. Zhiyi had no choice but to march; he met the enemy, won at first, then lost; Shougui hid the defeat and reported a victory. Word of the affair spread; the Emperor sent Palace Insider Supervisor Niu Xiantong to look into it. Shougui paid Xiantong a heavy bribe, pinned the crime on Bai Zhentuoluo, and forced him to hang himself. Xiantong enjoyed the Emperor's favor; the other eunuchs resented him and together brought the matter to light. The Emperor flew into a rage; on jiaxu he ordered Yang Si'en to club him to death. Si'en trussed him up, beat him hundreds of strokes, cut out his heart, and ate his flesh. Shougui was demoted to prefect of Kuozhou. Grand Mentor of the Heir Xiao Song had once given Xiantong several qing of fine land south of the capital; Li Linfu exposed him, and Song was demoted to prefect of Qingzhou.
111
秋，八月，乙亥，磧西節度使蓋嘉運擒突騎施可汗吐火仙。 嘉運攻碎-{葉}-城，吐火仙出戰，敗走，擒之-{於}-賀邏嶺。 分遣疎勒鎭守使夫蒙靈察與拔汗那王阿悉爛達-{干}-潛引兵突入怛邏斯城，擒黑姓可汗爾微，遂入曳建城，取交河公主，悉收散-{發}-之民數萬以與拔汗那王，威震西陲。
In autumn, the eighth month, on yihai, Qixi military governor Gai Jiayun took the Turgesh qaghan Tuhuoxian prisoner. Jiayun assaulted Suyab; Tuhuoxian marched out, was beaten and fled, and was seized at Helu Ridge. He sent Khotan commissioner Fumeng Lingcha and Ferghana's king Ashilan Mohedagan to steal into Talas, seize Black-clan qaghan Erwei, enter Yejian, recover the Princess of Jiaohe, and rally tens of thousands of scattered subjects for the Ferghana king—his fame thundered across the western frontier.
112
壬午，吐蕃寇白草、安人等軍，隴右節度使蕭炅撃破之。
On renwu Tibet attacked the Baicao and Anren garrisons; Longyou military governor Xiao Jiong drove them off.
113
甲申，追謚孔子爲文宣王。 先是，祀先聖先師，周公南向，孔子東向坐。 -{制}-：「自今孔子南向坐，被王者之服，釋奠用宮懸。 」追贈弟子皆爲公、侯、伯。
On jiashen Confucius was posthumously titled King Wenxuan. Earlier, when sacrificing to the Former Sage and Former Teacher, the Duke of Zhou faced south and Confucius sat facing east. An edict declared: "Henceforth Confucius shall face south, wear a king's robes, and the libation sacrifice shall use the full palace orchestra. " His disciples were posthumously given ranks of duke, marquis, and earl.
114
九月，戊午，處木昆、鼠尼施、弓月等諸部先隸突騎施者，皆帥衆内附，仍請徙居安西管内。
In the ninth month, on wuwu, the Chumukun, Shunishi, Gongyue, and other tribes once under Turgesh all led their clans to submit and asked to move within the Anxi protectorate.
115
太子更名紹。
The Heir Apparent was given the new name Shao.
116
冬，十月，辛巳，改修東都明堂。
In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, the eastern capital's Bright Hall was rebuilt.
117
丙戌，上幸驪山温泉； 十一月，辛-{丑}-，還宮。
On bingxu the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li; in the eleventh month, on xinchou, he returned to the palace.
118
甲辰，明堂成。
On jiachen the Bright Hall was finished.
119
劍南節度使張宥，文吏不習軍旅，悉以軍政委團練副使章仇兼瓊。 兼瓊入奏事，盛言安戎城可取，上悅之。 丁巳，以宥爲光祿卿。 十二月，以兼瓊爲劍南節度使。
Jiannan military governor Zhang You, a clerk who knew nothing of war, handed all military affairs to training vice-commissioner Zhang Qiu Jianqiong. Jianqiong came to court and urged that Anrong city could be seized; the Emperor was delighted. On dingsi Zhang You was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness. In the twelfth month Jianqiong was appointed military governor of Jiannan.
120
初，睿宗喪既除，祫-{於}-太廟； 自是三年一祫，五年一禘。 是歳，夏既禘，冬又當祫。 太常議以爲祭數則瀆，請停今年祫祭，自是通計五年一祫、一禘； 從之。
Earlier, once mourning for Ruizong had ended, a collective sacrifice was held in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; thereafter a collective sacrifice came every three years and a greater di sacrifice every five. That year the di sacrifice had already been held in summer, yet winter again required the collective sacrifice. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that too many rites would profane the spirits and asked to skip this year's collective sacrifice; henceforth both would be counted together—one collective sacrifice and one di sacrifice every five years; The Emperor agreed.
121
春，正月，癸巳，上幸驪山温泉； 庚子，還宮。 二月，荊州長史張九齡卒。 上雖以九齡忤旨逐之，然終愛重其人，毎宰相-{薦}-士，輒問曰：「風度得如九齡不？ 」
In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li; on gengzi he returned to the palace. In the second month Zhang Jiuling, chief administrator of Jingzhou, died. Though the Emperor had driven Jiuling away for crossing him, he still esteemed the man; whenever a chancellor recommended an official he would ask, "Does his bearing match Jiuling's? "
122
三月，丁亥朔，日有食之。
In the third month, on the first day dinghai, the sun was eclipsed.
123
章仇兼瓊潛與安戎城中吐蕃翟都局及維州別駕董承晏結謀，使局開門引内唐兵，盡殺吐蕃將卒，使監察-{御}-史許遠將兵守之。 遠，敬宗之曾孫也。
Jianqiong secretly allied with the Tibetan Zhai Duju inside Anrong city and Weizhou vice-prefect Dong Chengyan; Duju opened the gates to Tang troops, who slaughtered every Tibetan officer and soldier, and Jianqiong put investigating censor Xu Yuan in command of the garrison. Xu Yuan was a great-grandson of Emperor Jingzong.
124
甲寅，蓋嘉運入獻捷。 上赦吐火仙罪，以爲左金吾大將軍。 嘉運請立阿史那懷道之子昕爲十姓可汗； 從之。 夏，四月，辛未，以昕妻李氏爲交河公主。
On jiayin Gai Jiayun came to court to report his victory. The Emperor pardoned Tuhuoxian and appointed him general of the Left Golden Crow Guard. Jiayun asked that Ashina Huaidao's son Xin be made qaghan of the Ten Surnames; The Emperor agreed. In summer, the fourth month, on xinwei Xin's wife Lady Li was made Princess of Jiaohe.
125
六月，吐蕃圍安戎城。
In the sixth month Tibet laid siege to Anrong city.
126
上嘉蓋嘉運之功，以爲河西、隴右節度使，使之經略吐蕃。 嘉運恃恩流連，不時-{發}-。 左丞相裴耀卿上疎，以爲：「臣近與嘉運同班，觀其舉措，誠勇烈有-{餘}-，然言氣矜誇，恐難成事。 昔莫敖忸-{於}-蒲騷之役，卒喪楚師； 今嘉運有驕敵之色，臣竊憂之。 況防秋非遠，未言-{發}-日，若臨事始去，則吏卒尚未相識，何以-{制}-敵！ 且將軍受命，鑿凶門而出； 今乃酣宴朝夕，殆非憂國愛人之心。 若不可改易，宜速遣進塗，仍乞聖恩嚴加訓勵。 」上乃趣嘉運行。 已而嘉運竟無功。
The Emperor praised Gai Jiayun's victories and made him military governor of Hexi and Longyou to direct operations against Tibet. Jiayun, secure in imperial favor, lingered at court and did not depart on time. Left Chancellor Pei Yaojing memorialized the throne: "I have lately served on the same roster as Jiayun and watched him closely: he is brave enough, yet his speech is proud and boastful; I fear he will not succeed. Long ago the Mo'ao underrated his foe at Pusao and lost the entire Chu army; now Jiayun wears the look of a man who scorns his foe; I am privately alarmed. Moreover autumn defense is near, yet no departure date has been set; if he waits until the crisis to leave, officers and men will still be strangers to one another—how then can he face the enemy! When a general takes command he is supposed to bore through the Gate of Omens and march; yet now he feasts day and night—hardly the mind of a man who cares for the realm and his soldiers. If he cannot mend his ways, send him on the road at once, and I beg Your Majesty to admonish him sharply. " The Emperor then pressed Jiayun to march. In the end Jiayun accomplished nothing.
127
秋，八月，甲戌，幽州奏破奚、契丹。
In autumn, the eighth month, on jiaxu, Youzhou reported victories over the Xi and Khitan.
128
冬，十月，甲子，上幸驪山温泉； 辛巳，還宮。
In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li; on xinsi he returned to the palace.
129
吐蕃寇安戎城及維州； -{發}-關中強騎救之，吐蕃引去。 更命安戎城曰平戎。
Tibet attacked Anrong city and Weizhou; the court sent strong Guanzhong cavalry to the rescue, and Tibet withdrew. Anrong city was renamed Pingrong, "Pacify the Barbarians."
130
十一月，罷牛仙客朔方、河東節度使。
In the eleventh month Niu Xianke was relieved of the Shuofang and Hedong commands.
131
突騎施莫賀達-{干}-聞阿史那昕爲可汗，怒曰：「首誅蘇祿，我之謀也； 今立史昕，何以賞我？ 」遂帥諸部叛。 上乃立莫賀達-{干}-爲可汗，使統突騎施之衆，命蓋嘉運招諭之。 十二月，乙卯，莫賀達-{干}-降。
Turgesh leader Mohedagan, learning that Ashina Xin had been made qaghan, raged: "I was first to plot Sulu's death; now you set up Shi Xin—what reward is that for me? " He then led the tribes in revolt. The Emperor then made Mohedagan qaghan over the Turgesh and ordered Gai Jiayun to win him back. In the twelfth month, on yimao, Mohedagan surrendered.
132
金城公主薨； 吐蕃告喪，且請和，上不許。
Princess Jincheng died; Tibet announced her death and asked for peace; the Emperor refused.
133
是歳，天下縣千五百七十三，戸八百四十一萬二千八百七十一，口四千八百一十四萬三千六百九。 西京、東都米斛直錢不滿二百，絹匹亦如之。 海内富安，行者雖萬-{里}-不持寸兵。
That year the realm had 1,573 counties, 8,412,871 households, and 48,143,609 people. In Chang'an and Luoyang a hu of rice cost under two hundred cash, and silk by the bolt the same. The realm was rich and at peace; a traveler might go ten thousand li without bearing a weapon.
134
春，正月，癸巳，上幸驪山温泉。
In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li.
135
丁酉，-{制}-：「承前諸州饑饉，皆待奏報，然始開倉賑給。 道路悠遠，何救懸絶！ 自今委州縣長官與採訪使量事給訖奏聞。 」
On dingyou an edict declared: "In the past, when prefectures suffered famine, relief waited on memorials reaching the throne before granaries opened. The roads are long—how can that save men at the edge of death! Henceforth let prefectural and county officials and the investigation commissioners dispense relief as needed and report afterward. "
136
庚子，上還宮。 上夢玄元皇帝告-{云}-：「吾有像在京城西南百-{餘}--{里}-，汝遣人求之，吾當與汝興慶宮相見。 」上遣使求得之-{於}-盩厔樓觀山間。 夏，閏四月，迎置興慶宮。 五月，命畫玄元眞容，分置諸州開元觀。
On gengzi the Emperor returned to the palace. The Emperor dreamed that the Supreme Emperor of the Dark Origin said to him: "My image lies more than a hundred li southwest of the capital; send men to find it, and I shall meet you at Xingqing Palace. " He sent envoys, who found it in the Louguan hills of Zhouzhi. In summer, in the intercalary fourth month, the image was brought to Xingqing Palace. In the fifth month he ordered portraits of the Dark Origin painted and sent to the Kaiyuan abbeys in every prefecture.
137
六月，吐蕃四十萬衆入寇，至安仁軍，渾崖峰騎將臧希液帥衆五千撃破之。
In the sixth month four hundred thousand Tibetans invaded as far as Anren Army; cavalry commander Zang Xiye of Hunyafeng led five thousand men and routed them.
138
秋，七月，丙寅，突厥遣使來告登利可汗之喪。 初，登利從叔二人，分典兵馬，號左、右殺。 登利患兩殺之專，與其母謀，誘右殺，斬之，自將其衆。 左殺判闕特勒兵攻登利，殺之，立毘伽可汗之子爲可汗； 俄爲骨咄-{葉}-護所殺，更立其弟； 尋又殺之，骨咄-{葉}-護自立爲可汗。 上以突厥内亂，癸酉，命左羽林將軍孫老奴招諭回紇、葛邏祿、拔悉密等部落。
In autumn, the seventh month, on bingyin, the Turks sent envoys to announce Qaghan Dengli's death. Earlier Dengli had two younger uncles who each commanded troops, known as the Left and Right Shas. Dengli resented the Shas' power; with his mother he lured the Right Sha, killed him, and took command of his men. The Left Sha Pankue led his army against Dengli, killed him, and set up a son of Qaghan Pijia as qaghan; soon Kutlug Yabghu killed him and set up his younger brother; then killed him as well and made himself qaghan. Seeing the Turks in civil war, on guiyou the Emperor ordered Left Forest Guard general Sun Laonu to win over the Uyghurs, Qarluqs, Basmyls, and other tribes.
139
乙亥，東都洛水溢，溺死者千-{餘}-人。
On yihai the Luo River flooded Luoyang; more than a thousand drowned.
140
平盧兵馬使安祿山，傾巧，善事人，人多譽之。 上左右至平盧者，祿山皆厚賂之，由是上益以爲賢。 -{御}-史中丞張利貞爲河北採訪使，至平盧。 祿山-{曲}-事利貞，乃至左右皆有賂。 利貞入奏，盛稱祿山之美。 八月，乙未，以祿山爲營州都督，充平盧軍使，兩蕃、勃海、黑水四府經略使。
Pinglu army horse commander An Lushan was cunning, knew how to please men, and many praised him. Every courtier who visited Pinglu Lushan paid lavishly; the Emperor came to think him ever more able. Censor-in-Chief Zhang Lizhen, Hebei investigation commissioner, visited Pinglu. Lushan waited on Lizhen with every courtesy; even Lizhen's attendants were bribed. Lizhen returned to court and praised Lushan at length. In the eighth month, on yiwei, Lushan was made protector of Yingzhou, Pinglu army commander, and commissioner over the Two Fan, Bohai, and Heishui circuits.
141
冬，十月，丙申，上幸驪山温泉。
In winter, the tenth month, on bingshen, the Emperor went to the hot springs at Mount Li.
142
壬寅，分北庭、安西爲二節度。
On renyin Beiting and Anxi were split into two separate commands.
143
十一月，庚戌，司空邠王守禮薨。 守禮庸鄙無-{才}-識，毎天將雨及霽，守禮必先言之，已而皆驗。 岐、薛諸王言-{於}-上曰：「邠兄有-{術}-。 」上問其故，對曰：「臣無-{術}-。 則天時以章懷之故，幽閉宮中十-{餘}-年，歳賜敕杖者數四，背瘢甚厚，將雨則沉悶，將霽則輕爽，臣以此知之耳。 」因流涕沾襟； 上亦爲之慘然。
In the eleventh month, on gengxu, Minister of Works Prince Bin Shouli died. Shouli was mediocre and dull-witted; yet whenever rain was coming or the sky was about to clear, he always announced it first—and he was invariably right. The princes of Qi and Xue told the Emperor: "Our elder brother of Bin has supernatural skill. " When the Emperor asked why, he answered: "I have no such arts. In Empress Wu's time, because of Crown Prince Zhanghuai, I was confined in the palace for more than ten years and was caned by imperial order several times a year until my back was thick with scars. When rain was coming I felt heavy and oppressed; when the sky was about to clear I felt light and refreshed. I knew the weather only from that. " He wept until his robe was soaked; and the Emperor was deeply moved.
144
辛酉，上還宮。
On xinyou the Emperor returned to the palace.
145
辛未，太尉-{寧}-王憲薨。 上哀惋特甚，曰：「天下，兄之天下也； 兄固讓-{於}-我，爲唐太伯，常名不足以處之。 」乃謚曰讓皇帝。 其子汝陽王璡，上表追述先-{志}-謙-{沖}-，不敢當帝號； 上不許。 敛日，内出服，以手書致-{於}-靈座，書稱「隆基白」； 又名其墓曰惠陵，追謚其妃元氏曰恭皇-{后}-，附葬焉。
On xinwei Grand Preceptor Prince Ning Li Xian died. The Emperor grieved with exceptional sorrow and said: "The realm was my brother's realm; my brother firmly yielded it to me and was the Taibo of Tang—no ordinary title could do him justice. " He thereupon gave him the posthumous title Emperor Rang. His son, Prince of Ruyang Li Jin, memorialized that his father had been humble and yielding in life and that the family dared not accept an imperial title; the Emperor refused. On the day the body was laid in state he sent mourning garments from within the palace and wrote in his own hand to the spirit seat, signing himself "Respectfully, Longji"; he named the tomb Huiling, posthumously titled his consort Lady Yuan as Empress Gong, and had her buried there with him.
146
十二月，乙巳，吐蕃屠達化縣，陷石堡城，蓋嘉運不能-{御}-。
In the twelfth month, on yisi, Tibet massacred Dahua County, captured Shibao Fortress, and Gai Jiayun could not drive them off.
147
